source: generic ad-delivery taxonomy (no app-specific catalog ships with SeamHunter)
note: The `apps` map is intentionally empty. Populate it locally with your own fingerprints to enable known-app drift checks; nothing app-specific is distributed.

ima-dai.label: Google IMA / DAI client SDK
ima-dai.shape: The app's player asks Google's IMA SDK (client-side) or DAI (server-stitched pods) for ad breaks. The ad schedule surfaces in Java/Kotlin as cue points, ad-break lists or an AdsManager.
ima-dai.portable_seams: Cue-point / ad-break accessors, AdsManager.start, the SSAI AdsLoader getter, and live-pod handling are the usual crossing points. Seams found in one IMA app usually resemble the next.

ssai-manifest.label: Server-side stitching (SSAI) via manifest
ssai-manifest.shape: The CDN stitches ads into the stream itself. The only client-visible trace is the manifest (ad periods, DateRanges, ID3/beacon tags) and the host names that serve it.
ssai-manifest.portable_seams: The manifest and its origin/CDN hosts; ad periods and DateRange markers; for live passthrough SSAI the break boundary is the only client-side signal.

proprietary.label: Proprietary native / JS ad engine
proprietary.shape: The ad decision lives in the app's own runtime — a native library, a JS VM inside a .so, or a WebView — not in a standard SDK.
proprietary.portable_seams: Where the ad schedule crosses into the player (a response buffer, a JS function, an insertion-point accessor); native seams differ per build.
